title: Tetravox ViewSpec v2 — the host-facing subset (embed protocol 3)
description: THE HOST-FACING SUBSET of ARCHITECTURE.md 4.6's ViewSpec, hand-maintained. It covers what a host writes by hand and validates it strictly enough to catch a typo; it is NOT the full spec. Two differences from a *.tetravox.json on disk. (1) `datasets[].path` is a URL, not a path relative to a scene file — absolute http(s) is used as-is, anything else is resolved against LoadMessage.baseUrl. (2) Only `datasets` and `layers` are required: the nine view fields the engine requires (slices, view3d, layout, cursor, radiological, background, lighting, annotations, transparency) are filled from the engine's own empty scene when a host omits them, and a layer needs only id, datasetId and kind — every other field falls back to the engine's per-dataset default. FOUR LAYER KINDS, and the distinction between three of them is the point: `volume` is a NIfTI/MGZ scalar or label volume; `mesh` is a TETRAHEDRAL FEM volume (a SimNIBS .msh with element fields, tissue tags and an interior to cut open); `surface` is a TRIANGULAR two-dimensional sheet (FreeSurfer lh.pial/rh.white/lh.central, GIfTI .gii, STL/PLY/OBJ), which has no tags, no caps and no 2-D fill, and arrived with embed protocol 3 / Tetravox 0.4.0; `points` is written inline and arrived with protocol 2. Fields not listed here are still accepted and passed through unchanged; see ARCHITECTURE.md 4.4 for the complete layer model. A layer `kind` NOT listed here is the one thing the embed refuses outright, with an error naming the four.

version.description: Optional. Defaults to this build's SCENE_VERSION. This is the SCENE version and has nothing to do with the embed protocol number, which is 3.

activeLayerId.description: One of the layers' `id`s, or null.

kind.description: `volume` is a NIfTI/MGZ. `mesh` is a TETRAHEDRAL FEM mesh (.msh). `surface` is a TRIANGULAR surface — FreeSurfer binary (lh.pial, rh.white, lh.central — often with NO extension at all), GIfTI (.gii), or an STL/PLY/OBJ/OFF/.vtp shell. `surface` is a HOST-FACING SPELLING OF `mesh`, added by embed protocol 3: ARCHITECTURE.md 4.6's DatasetRef has only volume|mesh, because the engine decides surface-ness from the bytes (a mesh dataset with nTets === 0 IS a surface), and the embed maps `surface` down to `mesh` before the engine sees the ref. It exists so a host does not have to write `kind: 'mesh'` on a dataset whose layer is `kind: 'surface'`. Sending `mesh` for a surface file keeps working and loads identically. THIS IS NOT A FORMAT HINT — see `path`.

name.description: What the layer panel calls it.

path.description: Absolute http(s) URL, or relative/root-relative resolved against LoadMessage.baseUrl (default: the embed document's baseURI). THE FILE FORMAT IS READ FROM THE BYTES, NOT FROM THIS STRING: tvx_mesh_io::sniff tries $MeshFormat, VTK, MEDIT, GIfTI's XML, VTK-XML, OFF, PLY, STL and FreeSurfer's 24-bit big-endian magic in that order, and only falls back to the extension when none of them answers. That is why there is no `format: 'freesurfer' | 'gifti'` field here — the loader would not read it — and it is why the extensionless FreeSurfer surfaces work.

fingerprint.description: Optional. '' is exact for an embed: it is computed in the worker over bytes a host has never seen, and identifies a file only for a relocate dialog an embed does not have.

sidecars.description: Resolved against the DATASET's own URL, not the page: a sidecar travels with the file it describes (ARCHITECTURE.md 4.6). Reading one is best-effort — a missing sidecar is a missing table, never a failed load.

lut.description: A label volume's colour/name table, e.g. final_tissues_LUT.txt.

opt.description: A Gmsh .msh.opt — the only source of tissue names for a mesh with no $PhysicalNames.

fields.description: SURFACES ONLY, and new in embed protocol 3. Per-vertex files attached to the surface after it opens (ARCHITECTURE.md 4.6's third sidecar role, Engine.attachSurfaceData): a FreeSurfer .annot, a morph file (.thickness, .curv, .sulc, .area, .sulc), or a data-only GIfTI (.func.gii, .shape.gii, .label.gii). AN ARRAY, AND THE ORDER MATTERS — they are attached in it. Each becomes a field/label table named after ITS OWN FILE (`lh.ernie_DK40.annot`, never `annot`), which is the name a SurfaceLayer's `overlay.name` / `annotation.name` must use, and which is what lets two atlases on one hemisphere coexist. Best-effort like lut and opt: one that 404s is a missing table, never a failed load — so a surface whose annotation did not resolve opens SOLID, with a successful `loaded`.

VolumeLayer.title: VolumeLayer
VolumeLayer.description: A NIfTI/MGZ volume — a scalar (T1, a TI_max field) or a label volume with its LUT sidecar.

id.description: Host-chosen. NOT the id you get back: Engine.load reassigns every id.

scale.description: ARCHITECTURE.md 4.2. Omit it: a volume gets its own 2nd-98th percentile window, and a mesh field layer is windowed from that field's stats by the embed.

threshold.description: JSON has no infinity: an unset bound is written as null and read back as the infinity it stands for.

softEdge.description: Alpha ramp width as a fraction of hi-lo; 0 is a hard discard.

interpolation.description: Forced to nearest for a label volume.

MeshLayer.title: MeshLayer
MeshLayer.description: A TETRAHEDRAL FEM MESH — a SimNIBS .msh with element fields, tissue tags and an interior to cut open. NOT a triangular surface: from embed protocol 3 a FreeSurfer or GIfTI surface is `kind: 'surface'` (see SurfaceLayer), which has one colour source and no tags, caps, isolation or 2-D fill. Sending a surface file as `mesh` still loads and still draws — the renderer uses the same 7.4 triangle passes for both — but the layer then carries a tet mesh's whole vocabulary, two thirds of which is inert on a sheet.

id.description: Host-chosen. NOT the id you get back: Engine.load reassigns every id.

scale.description: ARCHITECTURE.md 4.2. Omit it: a volume gets its own 2nd-98th percentile window, and a mesh field layer is windowed from that field's stats by the embed.

threshold.description: JSON has no infinity: an unset bound is written as null and read back as the infinity it stands for.

softEdge.description: Alpha ramp width as a fraction of hi-lo; 0 is a hard discard.

field.description: Which field colours the mesh. `source` is where it lives in the file.

component.description: 'mag' or a 0-based component index for a vector field.

tagStyle.description: Per-tag visibility and opacity, keyed by the tag NUMBER as a string. Tags are not contiguous and a SimNIBS simulation mesh adds electrode/gel tags in the 101/501/1101/2101 ranges.

caps.description: Fill the cut with exact cap geometry.

contoursIn2D.description: Draw the mesh as outlines in the slice panes.

SurfaceLayer.title: SurfaceLayer
SurfaceLayer.description: A TRIANGULAR SURFACE (embed protocol 3, Tetravox 0.4.0) — ARCHITECTURE.md 4.4's SurfaceLayer as a host writes one. A surface is a triangle sheet with NO TETRAHEDRA: a hemisphere from a FreeSurfer binary (lh.pial, rh.white, lh.central) or a GIfTI (lh.pial.gii), an STL/PLY/OBJ shell, a .vtp. A MeshLayer is the other thing: a TETRAHEDRAL FEM volume, a SimNIBS .msh with element fields, tissue tags and an interior to cut open. The renderer draws both with the same 7.4 triangle passes, deliberately; the difference is the MODEL. A surface has no tissue tags, no isolation, no glyphs, no 2-D fill and NO CAPS (a sheet has no interior to cap), so tagStyle, clip.caps, fillIn2D and `field` are absent from this definition rather than accepted and ignored. What it has instead is exactly ONE COLOUR SOURCE at a time, chosen by colorMode: a solid colour, a per-vertex `overlay` (curvature, thickness, a .func.gii) or a per-vertex `annotation` (a .annot or .label.gii atlas). Before protocol 3 a .gii had to be sent as kind:'mesh'; that still loads and still draws — it is the model that was wrong, not the picture.

id.description: Host-chosen. NOT the id you get back: Engine.load reassigns every id.

datasetId.description: Must match a DatasetRef.id in `datasets`. That ref's kind may be `surface` or `mesh`.

colorMode.description: Which colour source is live. Absent is 'solid'. THESE ARE NOT THE MESH NAMES: a MeshLayer says 'field' and 'tag', a surface says 'overlay' and 'annotation'. 'overlay' with no `overlay`, or 'annotation' with no `annotation`, falls back to 'solid' rather than failing.

solidColor.description: 0..1 RGBA, drawn when colorMode is 'solid'. OMITTING BOTH THIS AND contourColor takes a palette entry BY LOAD ORDER — first surface Freeview yellow [1, 0.9, 0.15, 1], then green, orange, periwinkle, rose, teal, wrapping at six. A nicety for two hemispheres and a trap for a host that expected a fixed colour: name one if you care.

overlay.description: The per-vertex SCALAR that colours the surface when colorMode is 'overlay' — curvature, thickness, a .func.gii, a morph file. `name` is the field's name in the dataset, which for a file attached through sidecars.fields is THAT FILE'S OWN BASE NAME (`lh.thickness`). There is no `source` field: a surface's data is per-vertex by construction, which is the `source: 'node'` a MeshLayer has to say out loud (a .msh simulation field is usually 'elm'). Window it with colormap / scale / threshold below.

component.description: 'mag' (the default, and all a scalar has) or a 0-based component index for a vector.

annotation.description: The per-vertex ATLAS that colours the surface when colorMode is 'annotation' — a FreeSurfer .annot, a .label.gii, or a <LabelTable> the geometry file carried. `name` is the field's name in the dataset: for an attached file, that file's own base name (`lh.ernie_DK40.annot`). THERE IS NO `table` HERE and there must not be: 4.4's LabelTable is the one non-JSON field, re-derived from the dataset by `name` on load, and a host has never seen the colours inside the .annot it is naming. A name that matches nothing does NOT fail the load — the layer falls back to colorMode 'solid' and its palette colour, and the `layers` event is where you find out.

mode.description: How the parcels are drawn. Absent is 'fill'.

visibleLabels.description: A whitelist of label ids. Absent means all.

colormap.description: Colours an `overlay`. An `annotation` is drawn through its own table instead.

colormapNegative.description: A second ramp for the negative half of a signed overlay.

scale.description: ARCHITECTURE.md 4.2. Omit it: a volume gets its own 2nd-98th percentile window, and a mesh field layer is windowed from that field's stats by the embed.

threshold.description: JSON has no infinity: an unset bound is written as null and read back as the infinity it stands for.

softEdge.description: Alpha ramp width as a fraction of hi-lo; 0 is a hard discard.

faceMode.description: Forced to 'both' for a surface with open edges, whatever this says.

edges.description: A BOOLEAN here, not the MeshLayer's { surface, caps } object: a sheet has no caps.

clip.description: PLANES ONLY. A MeshLayer's `caps` and `capColorMode` are absent by design: a sheet has no interior for a cap to fill.

contoursIn2D.description: ABSENT IS TRUE here, unlike a MeshLayer. A surface's whole 2-D presence is its outline; without it a surface is invisible in the slice panes.

PointsLayer.title: PointsLayer
PointsLayer.description: A points layer written INLINE (protocol 2). There is no points file an embed could serve, so the coordinates arrive with the layer: `datasetId` names a dataset already in this spec — the volume the points sit over — exactly as the sEEG contact editor hangs its contacts off the CT they were localised on. `state` and `labelMode` are this protocol's own vocabulary and are resolved before the engine sees the layer; everything else is ARCHITECTURE.md 4.4's PointsLayer verbatim.

datasetId.description: A dataset in THIS spec. Points need no file, but a layer needs a carrier (4.4).

pickable.description: Whether 7.2.3's id pass answers for this layer. The point tool hit-tests regardless.

shape.description: 'sphere' (default) is radiusMm in world mm; 'dot' is a constant screen size in BOTH the 2-D slice panes and the 3-D pane (the 3-D half arrived in Tetravox 0.3.12; before it, a 3-D pane drew millimetre spheres whatever this said). A 3-D dot is flat, not shaded.

radiusMm.description: Default 4 mm, about an EEG electrode.

color.description: 0..1 RGBA — every point with neither its own colour nor a resolved state.

labelMode.description: Default 'none'. 'names' draws each point's own name at its own position; 'labels' draws the layer's free-standing labels[] anchors, which only a parsed Gmsh view has. There is no 'hover': the engine draws no hover text, and a mode that silently did nothing would be worse than its absence.

stateColors.description: What each points[].state paints, when that point carries no explicit color. Absent states keep the default: idle -> the layer colour, selected -> [1, 0.8, 0.2, 1] (rgb 255,204,51), disabled -> [0.6, 0.6, 0.6, 1] (rgb 153,153,153). `idle` was accepted and ignored before Tetravox 0.3.12; from 0.3.12 an idle point with no color of its own takes it.

offPlaneOpacity.description: How visible a point is in a 2-D pane it is not on. 0 or absent is 7.2's hard cull — right for a scalp net, wrong for a depth electrode, whose shaft no single slice contains.

dotRadiusPx.description: shape 'dot' only: the screen radius in CSS pixels. Absent is 4.

Point.title: Point
Point.description: One point. Unlisted fields are accepted and passed through — 4.4 is the complete model.

id.description: The point's identity, and what a `pick` event and `setPointSelection` name it by. Optional — the engine mints `p<index>` for a point with none, and an index moves when a point is deleted, so send your own if you want to recognise your electrode.

state.description: Resolved to a colour from stateColors above, including 'idle' (from Tetravox 0.3.12; before that 'idle' was never state-coloured). An explicit `color` on the same point wins. Not the tool selection: any number of points may be selected here, exactly one can be the selection.
